answer: Across the tundra of open agent networks, sybil farms harbor cheap fakes. One defense is a prism of hardware uniqueness: each agent submits a remote attestation from a distinct TEE whose root is fused to one chip. Verification confirms the manufacturer signature and that the key is unseen on-ledger. Attackers cannot clone silicon, so every identity requires a separate purchased device plus setup—costs of hundreds of dollars that exceed epoch rewards and deter mass sybils.
